jurisdiction.name: Houston
jurisdiction.notes: City of Houston (mostly Harris County; parts extend into Fort Bend and Montgomery). Houston has no zoning: land use is controlled by recorded deed restrictions, Chapter 42 development rules and Chapter 26 parking, plus TABC distance rules for alcohol. Most permits are filed at the Houston Permitting Center (1002 Washington Ave.); food permits are processed by the Houston Health Department at 8000 N. Stadium Dr. Mobile food units have been licensed by Texas DSHS since July 1, 2026; the Houston Fire Marshal still inspects them.

permits.name: Land-use check: deed restrictions, Chapter 42 / Chapter 26 parking and alcohol distance rules (Houston has no zoning)
permits.issuing_agency: Houston Planning & Development Department (site plan review) + recorded deed restrictions
permits.notes: Houston does not zone land uses, but recorded deed restrictions can prohibit restaurants or bars and the City enforces them: building permits and food permits for new construction or change of use require a deed restrictions declaration. Site plans are checked against Chapter 42 (setbacks, access, platting) and Chapter 26 off-street parking. For alcohol, TABC and City rules bar sales within 300 ft of a church (door to door) or school or public hospital (property line), so pull a title report and run the distances before signing a lease.
permits.stall_risk: A deed restriction or a parking shortfall discovered after lease signing can kill a site or force a costly parking agreement. Order the title commitment with restrictions and a parking count during due diligence.

permits.name: Alcoholic beverage location review + City Secretary execution of the TABC application
permits.issuing_agency: Houston Administration & Regulatory Affairs (ARA) – Commercial Permitting & Enforcement; Office of the City Secretary
permits.notes: After preparing the TABC application (L-ON for on-premise), bring it to ARA at the Permitting Center for an onsite location review; the address must be posted at the proposed entrance. Routine reviews take 7–10 business days, and once the location is certified eligible you have under 60 days to get the City Secretary to execute the application. ARA's director's rule requires a sealed survey showing distances to churches, schools and public hospitals within 300 ft. The Harris County Clerk certifies county wet/dry status separately.
permits.stall_risk: A church or school inside 300 ft makes the location ineligible, and letting the 60-day certification window lapse means starting over. Commission the distance survey before signing the lease and calendar the City Secretary deadline.

permits.name: City of Houston local alcoholic beverage permit fee (Chapter 3)
permits.issuing_agency: Houston Administration & Regulatory Affairs – Commercial Permitting & Enforcement
permits.notes: Once TABC issues your permit, open a City fee account with your TABC permit number and Certificate of Occupancy number and pay the City's local fee; for a wine and beer retailer it runs $87.50–$500 depending on the original issue year, about 1 day in person or 3–5 days by mail, with an unannounced inspection after issuance. Mixed beverage permits carry a larger local fee (Texas lets cities charge up to half the state fee). Renew yearly alongside the TABC permit.

permits.name: Harris County local alcoholic beverage fee
permits.issuing_agency: Harris County Tax Assessor-Collector – Special Permit Taxes
permits.notes: Harris County Commissioners Court levies a local fee equal to one-half the state TABC fee, collected by the county Tax Office (e.g. $1,000 original / $750 renewal for an on-premise beer and wine retailer). New applicants are routed through TABC; renewals are paid by mail or at 1001 Preston and cannot be paid more than 30 days before the renewal date. Keep the receipt with your TABC records.

permits.name: Food establishment plan review (Houston Health Department)
permits.issuing_agency: Houston Health Department – Plan Review Section (at the Houston Permitting Center)
permits.notes: Required for new construction, converting a space that was not a food establishment, and remodels that move walls, floors or equipment or change the scope of food service. Submit two sets of scaled plans (equipment layout and specs, plumbing and equipment elevations, room-finish schedule) to the Health Department plan review desk on the 3rd floor of the Permitting Center alongside the building permit. Build exactly to the approved plans; deviations need re-approval before the pre-opening inspection.

permits.name: Food Dealer's Permit (food establishment operating permit)
permits.issuing_agency: Houston Health Department – Bureau of Consumer Health Services
permits.notes: Schedule the pre-operational inspection at least 14 business days ahead (832-393-5100) with stamped plans on site and the Certified Food Manager present; if you pass, you are invoiced and the permit is processed within about 15 business days at 8000 N. Stadium Dr. Since the Sept. 2025 switch to DSHS-style risk tiers the Health Department lists fees of $258 / $515 / $773 (low / medium / high risk) plus inspection and admin fees, although the Permitting Center listing still shows the older $224–$739 range. Renewed annually; keep the permit posted.
permits.stall_risk: The 14-business-day lead time for pre-opening inspections is easy to miss; book the inspection as soon as the construction finish date is firm, and have the CFM and stamped plans on site or the inspection is a fail.

permits.name: Commercial building permit (build-out / remodel / change of use / new building)
permits.issuing_agency: Houston Public Works – Houston Permitting Center, Building Code Enforcement (Commercial Plan Review)
permits.notes: Apply through iPermits and upload plans to ProjectDox with the Commercial Prerequisite Checklist (CE-1105) and the building permit declaration (CE-1380/1381). The build-out permit lists 15 business days per review, but restaurant kitchens and changes of use are excluded from the walk-in One-Stop track and every rejection adds a full review cycle. Fees follow the City fee schedule (raised 1.39% on Jan. 1, 2026) plus separate electrical, plumbing, mechanical and fire-suppression permits.
permits.stall_risk: Multiple rejection cycles across fire, MEP and health reviewers are the usual delay. Submit a complete set with the health plan review at the same time, and use the paid Expedited Review Service after the first full review if the schedule is tight.

permits.name: Certificate of Occupancy (new occupant, change of occupancy, or new building)
permits.issuing_agency: Houston Public Works – Houston Permitting Center, Occupancy Inspections
permits.notes: Houston requires a CO before any commercial space is occupied, a new one when the occupancy classification, square footage or occupant load changes, and a new one when a business moves to a different address. For an existing space email form CE-1045A to Occupancy Inspections, pay the same day via iPermits, and pass the inspection with power on and the space set up; certificates are emailed once the inspection is approved. Fees run $94–$537.12 depending on the project.
permits.stall_risk: Inspections fail when the space is not fully set up, power is off, or attic and roof access is not provided, and a no-show costs a $112.64 re-inspection. Apply only when the space is truly ready.

permits.name: Houston Fire Marshal place of assembly (P2) / occupant load permit
permits.issuing_agency: Houston Fire Department – Fire Marshal's Office, Life Safety Bureau (Fire Permits Office)
permits.notes: Restaurants, bars and venues with an occupant load of 50 or more need an annual place-of-assembly permit and a posted maximum occupancy from the Fire Marshal. File the Fire Prevention Permit Application with the unsworn declaration at the Permits Office (1002 Washington, 2nd floor); an inspector checks exits, signage, extinguishers and alarm systems. ARA will not issue a dance hall license without this permit.

permits.name: Type I hood fire suppression system permit and acceptance test
permits.issuing_agency: Houston Public Works – Building Code Enforcement (fire suppression plan review) + Houston Fire Marshal
permits.notes: Grease-producing cooking needs a Type I hood with a listed suppression system, permitted by a licensed fire-suppression contractor (the 2026 fee schedule lists roughly $98 per system plus minimum and admin fees) and acceptance-tested before the building final. Keep semi-annual service tags current; the Fire Marshal checks them on every inspection.

permits.name: Grease trap / FOG generator registration (food establishment)
permits.issuing_agency: Houston Health Department – Special Waste Program (with Houston Public Works pretreatment rules, Chapter 47)
permits.notes: Food establishments with a grease interceptor register as special waste generators in person at 8000 N. Stadium Dr. with the food dealer account number and an Affidavit of Holding Capacity; fee $123.54 plus a $33.56 admin fee, processed in about 10 minutes. The permit runs one year from the food dealer permit date and must be posted. Interceptors must be fully pumped at least quarterly by a licensed hauler, and the interceptor size itself is approved during building plan review.
permits.renewal: Annually with the food dealer permit

permits.name: On-premise commercial sign permit
permits.notes: Most signs must be permitted and installed by a licensed sign contractor (owners may do small non-electrical ground signs); processing takes 4–11 business days. Expect roughly $300 for a basic sign: $97.25 plan review, $97.25 inspection, a $69.46 annual operating fee and a $33.56 admin fee, plus per-square-foot charges above 32 sq ft and a sign electrical permit if illuminated. The operating permit renews annually (15% late fee).

permits.name: Commercial establishment sound (amplified sound) permit – Chapter 30 noise ordinance
permits.issuing_agency: Houston Administration & Regulatory Affairs – Commercial Permitting & Enforcement
permits.notes: A food or beverage business within 300 ft of a residence that plays amplified sound audible outside needs ARA's 12-month commercial establishment permit (since the 2022 amendments permits are issued to the establishment). Permitted sound may reach 75 dB(A) until 10 p.m. Sun–Thu and 11 p.m. Fri–Sat, with lower limits after that, and no amplified sound is allowed from 2 a.m. to 8 a.m. Two convictions in 36 months can lead to suspension or revocation, and citations run up to $2,000.

permits.name: Dance Hall License (Class A – nightclubs and venues with public dancing)
permits.issuing_agency: Houston Administration & Regulatory Affairs – Regulatory Permitting
permits.notes: Houston does license dance halls: any place where public dancing is allowed, including nightclubs, needs a Class A license ($964.95 + $32.16 admin; a one-night-per-week license is $353.81). Applicants need a criminal background check, a current CO, the P2 assembly fire permit and a food dealer's permit if food is served, and must post a dress code. ARA's review with Fire, Public Works and Health takes 4–6 weeks; renew annually.

permits.name: Sidewalk Café License (public right-of-way)
permits.issuing_agency: Houston Public Works – Houston Permitting Center (traffic engineer inspection)
permits.notes: Chapter 40 license for tables on the public sidewalk: $201.41 plus a $33.56 admin fee, renewed yearly for $100.71. The application needs a site plan by a registered surveyor or engineer, drawings of any temporary structures and the clear pedestrian path, seating counts, proof of ownership or authorization, your food establishment permit number, and $1M/$2M liability insurance naming the City. The license cannot be transferred to a new owner.

permits.name: City of Houston Hotel Occupancy Tax registration (7%, collected by Houston First)
permits.issuing_agency: Houston First Corporation (City of Houston HOT collection agent)
permits.notes: The City's 7% hotel occupancy tax is administered by Houston First: email hoteltax@houstonfirst.com with the registration form to get a City tax ID for a new hotel, or notify them if you bought an existing one. Reports and payments are due quarterly (Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31); late filing triggers 10% annual interest and a 15% penalty after a full quarter. This is in addition to the 6% state tax and the Harris County / Sports Authority taxes.

permits.name: Harris County and Houston Sports Authority hotel occupancy tax registration
permits.issuing_agency: Harris County Tax Assessor-Collector – Hotel/Motel Occupancy Tax
permits.notes: Harris County collects its own hotel tax plus the Harris County-Houston Sports Authority tax; inside Houston city limits the county portion is commonly cited as 2% with the Sports Authority adding about 2%, for roughly 17% combined with state and city taxes. Register by emailing the online-filing registration form (and new owner form) to hoteloccupancytax@tax.hctx.net to get a Hotel ID; file quarterly. Confirm the exact rates with the Tax Office (713-274-8151).

permits.name: Houston Fire Marshal food truck permit and inspection (LP-gas / cooking units)
permits.issuing_agency: Houston Fire Department – Fire Marshal's Office, Mobile Food Unit section
permits.notes: Food trucks operating in Houston are inspected by the Fire Marshal (7427 Park Place Blvd.); start by registering with DSHS, after which the Fire Marshal emails you to validate paperwork and book an inspection. LP-gas users need an annual L1 permit (or a temporary L3 for a single event). Every truck needs a 3A:40BC extinguisher, a Type K extinguisher if frying, a Type I hood with suppression for grease-laden vapors, secured upright cylinders with a leak detector, and must park 10 ft from buildings and 25 ft from other LP-gas trucks.

permits.name: Mobile food unit central preparation facility / servicing area (commissary) and restroom letter
permits.issuing_agency: Houston Health Department – Mobile Food Unit program (inspections on behalf of DSHS)
permits.notes: Houston mobile units must operate from an approved Central Preparation Facility and report daily to one of the City's approved servicing areas (only about 16 are permitted for water and liquid-waste service); grease must go to a facility holding a FOG permit. The Health Department now inspects on behalf of DSHS and still expects a restroom letter from a business within 500 meters of each location, commercial-grade equipment, a three-compartment sink and a wastewater tank 15% larger than the potable tank. Commissary rent is a recurring cost, not a permit fee.
permits.stall_risk: Servicing-area capacity is limited; secure a commissary contract before buying or wrapping the truck, because the DSHS pre-licensing inspection and Houston operations both depend on it.
